investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T07:01–07:09Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected for any check because the underlying VM pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod required by remote agent creation on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (resource quota exhausted or all slots in use), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-15T07:01–07:09Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected for any check because the underlying VM pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod required by remote agent creation on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (resource quota exhausted or all slots in use), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-15 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, while the remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent eval pod timed out unscheduled (~126–148 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream evidence collection impossible. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents eval path; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.

All three sibling checks report the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the eval pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, concentrating all remote-agent scheduling pressure onto those 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity problem.

[Possible] A concurrent workload or leaked eval pod from a prior run is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new pods from scheduling. The scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' suggests no lower-priority pods are present to evict, but other non-preemptible workloads could still be occupying slots.
[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration on the eval pod may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run kata peer-pods if the selector were relaxed.
